Fucks me up to no end seeing you guys attacking _kids_ who found out the hard way how student loans work, and not the _system_ that not only failed to educate them on how student loans work in the first place, but pressured them into going to college to take on loans their degrees would never pay off. 

It's all a lie by omission. Students were punished for seeking higher education after years of indoctrination from teachers simply saying "go to college because degree=higher paying job". They don't even teach you how student loans work, just that they exist. Nobody prepares you for the fact that you will be more likely unable to afford to pay more than interest than you are to pay off your student loans at all. That remains true for all degrees, just look around. Unless you got a free ride, massive scholarships, or very lucky, you're not safe. Just look at how many entry level jobs are out there 🤪.

And then you say "you still have to pay off your loans even after you declare bankruptcy" with a level of nonchalance that almost condones the corruption rather than educates about it. 

Anyone laughing at another's financial illiteracy over student loans is showing off their own blindness to the corruption of the system. At this point, I'd lean towards advising students not to go to college at all. Unless you have a _guarantee_ that you'll pay off anywhere between 25 to 100 thousand or more in loans, in a very short amount of time... It's literally not worth it. Look into trades.

comments.text: The student loan one makes me so sad -- people assume that because you filll out this form from the government that you aren't getting scammed. There's an air of authority. It's predatory. Thankfully I studied econ and chose a middle ground option bc I felt my college was still affordable if I end up paying 30k on 20k of loans. The other thing is unlike a mortgage you are NOT ALLOWED to elect that payments above and beyond your minimum go towards the premium. So someone like my husband who worked for a school and deferred paying but interest kept growing now has to pay down almost 5 figures of interest before he can even touch the principal. Crazy manipulative that you can't elect where the money goes.

comments.text: I started explaining the basics of interest to my elementary students. That it can work for you if you save early over a long period of time. If you need to have a loan check out the amortization schedule and pay as much over the minimum on principal as you can afford , because interest can’t be charged on principal that isn’t there. Check out the difference over time of paying off $40-$100 a month on principal ( mark it principal only) on an amortization schedule, it will be sizable savings.
